To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total concentrations of trace metals in the riparian zone of theDanube River are generally low, with the highest levels found at the confluence with the SavaRiver.

the levels of As, Cd, Cr and Hg were below the threshold values for soil quality in all samples, and only in a few samples of the riparian zone of the Danube did the concentrations of Cu, Ni, Pb, and Zn exceed these values.
the total levels of trace elements in riparian soils are generally lower than in the river sediments, while the concentrations of these metals in the riparian vegetation are higher than in the soils.
